shorts.title: City Orders Man to Hide His Boat — So He Paints It on the Fence 😂
shorts.description:
City Orders Man to Hide His Boat — So He Paints It on the Fence 😂

City Orders Man to Hide His Boat — So He Paints It on the Fence, sparking viral hilarity and widespread praise for ultimate compliance. Etienne Constable had parked his boat in the driveway of his Seaside, California home for years until he received a notice from the city requiring boats and trailers to be screened behind a six-foot fence to avoid fines.
Finding the rule frustrating yet wanting to stay law-abiding, Constable constructed the six-foot wooden fence as instructed. However, he then teamed up with his next-door neighbor, artist Hanif Panni, to paint a photorealistic, life-sized mural of the boat directly onto the new fence. From the street, the optical illusion makes it appear as though the fence doesn't exist and the boat is still sitting in plain view. The hilarious gesture quickly went viral across TikTok and Facebook, prompting other neighbors with boat notices to request their own custom murals. Constable explained he wanted to make a humorous statement while technically obeying the law, and Seaside’s acting city manager even congratulated him and gave him a high five.

shorts.description:
Little Girl Uses Display iPad for Homework — Employee’s Reaction Is Heartwarming 🥺

Little Girl Uses Display iPad for Homework — Employee’s Reaction Is Heartwarming, triggering millions of views and viral praise across social media platforms. The touching surveillance footage captures a young girl walking into a shopping mall carrying her backpack and stopping in front of an electronics display.
Without access to a computer or internet at home, she placed her bag on the floor, squatted down beside the stand, and began using the display iPad to complete her math assignment. A few moments later, a store worker approached and took the iPad back, leaving the quiet student to pack up her belongings and slowly walk away. However, what initially appeared to be a strict reprimand was actually a thoughtful act of compassion. The employee quickly called her back, carrying a small stool so she didn't have to crouch on the hard floor. Handing the iPad back to her, the staff member stayed beside her to guide her through her studies. The security camera clip went viral, with online viewers praising the worker's kindness toward a determined student.

shorts.title: The Gun That Fires Through Its Own Propeller
shorts.description:
In 1915 you aimed a fighter by pointing the whole plane, so the machine gun had to shoot straight through the spinning blades.

Pilots tried a gun on the top wing, and Roland Garros bolted steel wedges to his propeller so stray bullets bounced off. When his engine failed behind German lines, Fokker's engineers studied his plane and built something better: a cam on the engine that pushed a rod to fire the gun only when the blades were clear, about forty times a second. The test bench, the gear's proportions and the aircraft are illustrations, not replicas.

Sources: Wikipedia, "Synchronization gear"; Wikipedia, "Roland Garros (aviator)"; Wikipedia, "Louis Strange"
